The Predators are 7-4-5, and those five overtime losses tell you how they've lived: close games, a point most nights, a lot of hockey decided late. They've won three straight now, outscoring teams 12-7 on 54% of the expected goals, which is the best stretch of process they've put together.

The season-long picture is thinner. Nashville gets 46% of the five-on-five expected goals, and our numbers count about two points of luck in the standings. Juuse Saros is the reason it hasn't been worse. Over his last five starts he's 3.8 goals saved above expected, and North State Journal's Cory Lavalette wrote after the Nov. 4 win over Carolina, "Saros was great."

The most effective line has been the grinders: Ross Colton, Jack Drury and Adam Edstrom at 62% of the chances. The veteran unit of Steven Stamkos, Ryan O'Reilly and Mavrik Bourque is at 47%, and it's been outscored 3-1. Roman Josi and Adam Wilsby are a 56% pair, while Brady Skjei and Nick Perbix have struggled (44%, outscored 8-5).

The roster is moving, too. The Predators sent Matthew Wood to Seattle for Shane Wright on Nov. 1, so the Filip Forsberg line will look different. Vitali Pinchuck scored his first NHL goal this week. Our numbers have Nashville at 51% for the playoffs, the definition of a bubble team.
headline: Nashville is hanging in on Saros and loser points
